title: Cap. VIII: prefatory — not the will to damn, but the eternal denial of efficacious grace
pass_a_gloss: But before the reasons of these are brought into the midst, this is to be prefaced: That it is not asked concerning reprobation, insofar as it denotes among some Theologians the will of damning or of tormenting the reprobated: For it ought to be outside controversy that this will of God always regards sin as the meritorious cause of the decreed punishment. But it is asked concerning reprobation, insofar as it denotes that absolute and eternal decree of God, by which from eternity he denied to Cain and Judas efficacious grace, which he could have prepared and given them, if it had so pleased him.
pass_b_english: Before their reasons are brought forward, this must be prefaced: we are not asking about reprobation as some theologians mean the will to damn or torment the reprobate — that will of God always regards sin as meritorious cause of decreed punishment, beyond dispute. We ask about reprobation as that absolute eternal decree by which from eternity God denied Cain and Judas efficacious grace he could have prepared and given them, had it so pleased him.
source_text: Sed priusquam horum rationes in medium afferantur, id praestruendum est: Non quaeri de reprobatione, quatenus denotat apud nonnullos Theologos voluntatem damnandi sive cruciandi reprobatos: Nam extra controversiam esse debet, hanc voluntatem Dei semper respicere peccatum ut meritoriam causam decretae punitionis. Sed quaeritur de reprobatione, quatenus denotat absolutum illud et aeternum Dei decretum, quo negavit ab aeterno Caino et Judae efficacem gratiam, quam illis praeparare et dare potuisset, si ita illi complacitum fuisset.
